scope: Only the robots-policy 820 ms observation is replaced. The original 800 ms native fetch, 250 ms page budget, concurrency 1, all real Chrome/HTTP paths and all original 14 cases/66 expectations remain. The pacing 1300 ms window is unchanged.
method: Five bounded commands, shared benchmark lock, own checkout/dependencies. No native operation promise is replaced: synchronous case-local forUrl/newPage/request-listener forwarding returns each exact original result. Same attached connection and exact native target object correlate destruction. Actual forbidden HTTP arrival is an escape to the original no-hit oracle. Original 45 matcher/13 name expressions retained; 31 awaits remain, with only the 820 ms await replaced.

runtime.isolation: Required Chrome flag and original preload plus explicit ordinary-UID user/network namespace with loopback only, no external route, and capabilities dropped before test process. Native launch flags unchanged. No app build required by this file.
runtime.resources: GNU time inside shared benchmark lock, after namespace setup. Shared-host background load uncontrolled; process-tree peak RSS is not summed memory. Setup and original820 ms elapsed span were not separately measured.

allRequired: The original matching robots.forUrl promise settles, including parsing/cache completion.
The original matching main-frame interception listener promise settles, including continue/abort await.
The same native page target emits targetdestroyed on the same attached Browser connection.
completion.escape: Only an actual matching /late HTTP arrival lets the original no-hit assertion decide before missing destruction. No null/quiet/timeout fallback.
completion.fault: Remove cancellation forwarding into actual clearToFetch, its post-policy abort guard, and actual finally page.close together. Budget controller and actual native dispatch remain. Each guard is independently protective; this compound fault does not inject a request.
completion.limits: Completion is for this original load and its shared policy work, not all browser/network activity. The native 800 ms fetch remains. The 1300 ms pacing window also permits actual 1200 ms eligibility before the next 300 ms budget; target/handler completion alone does not replace it.
